$comment: JSON Schema for the `manifest.toml` of an agent package, mirroring the main repo's `acowork_core::AgentManifest` (core/acowork-core/src/manifest.rs). This file is a MIRROR, not an invention: every property here exists in the main repo with the same name, type and constraint. Community-specific metadata does NOT live here — it lives in `hub.json` (see schema/hub.schema.json), because the main repo re-serialises the parsed manifest on clone/upgrade and would silently drop unknown top-level fields.
title: Agent package manifest.toml
description: Schema for agents/<owner>/<name>/manifest.toml, parsed from TOML into JSON before validation. This is a faithful mirror of the main repo's AgentManifest; it must not drift from it.

agent_id.description: Reverse-domain package identity, e.g. `com.example.weather`. The main repo requires a `.` in the value. This is PACKAGE identity only — never a runtime instance id.

display_name.description: Short display name for chat UI. Defaults to `name` when absent.

role.description: Agent role / job title, e.g. `Project Manager`. Shown in the UI. The hub requires this for community agents — it is core identity information, not decoration.

avatar.description: Path to an avatar image inside the package, e.g. `assets/avatar.png`. Highest priority; falls back to `builtin_avatar`, then to a random bundled icon.

builtin_avatar.description: Bundled avatar index chosen at packaging time, e.g. `icon-05` or `5`.

description.description: Short description of what the agent does.

runtime_version.description: Minimum compatible Agent Runtime version, e.g. `0.1.0`.

labels.description: Retrieval / discovery tags (ADR-104). A label is a filter dimension only — not a capability, not a skill name, not the role. The hub derives the browse category from these via the label->category map in schema/catalog.json.

identity_deps.description: System Agent identity fields this agent depends on, e.g. `["language", "timezone"]`.

permissions.description: Declared permissions. The main repo rejects unknown permission types outright, so this enum is exact.

value.description: Optional scope: a URL for Network, a path for the filesystem permissions, an agent id for the intent permissions, a URL pattern for RagQuery.

tools.description: Builtin tool opt-in declarations (ADR-029). Each entry seeds `agent_tools.json` with `enabled = true` on first start.

type.description: Tool type. `builtin` for the runtime's built-in tools, `rag` for an enterprise RAG endpoint.

rag.description: RAG configuration. Only meaningful when `type` is `rag`.

mcp_servers.description: Recommended MCP servers (ADR-104). A recommendation, not a dependency: the user confirms installation and activation. Each entry must pick exactly ONE form — `preset`, `hosted`, or an inline remote endpoint. Inline stdio is rejected by the main repo, because a package must not name an executable to run on the user's machine.

name.description: Explicit identity key. Defaults to the preset / hosted id.

preset.description: Platform preset id from the MCP preset registry.

transport.description: Transport for the inline form. `stdio` is not allowed in a package.

url.description: Inline remote endpoint URL. Must be http(s) and covered by a `Network` permission.

required.description: Soft requirement: unmet never blocks startup. The gap is shown in the Tools panel.

why.description: Author's reason, shown verbatim in the Tools panel.

capabilities.description: Capability advertisements for Intent routing. A capability is an outward contract other agents address through an intent; a skill is an internal workflow. The relation is many-to-many via `skills`.

skills.description: Skills that implement this capability. Documentation and validation link only — the runtime does not load a skill because it is listed here.

llm.description: LLM configuration. Provider and model selection is governed globally by the Gateway, not by the manifest.

resources.description: Resource limits for the agent process.

skills.description: Skill injection mode. `progressive = true` injects a compact summary of available skills into the system prompt.

config.description: Package-author defaults for `agent_config.json` (ADR-104). Seeded by the Runtime on first start; never overwrites a value the user already set.

dev.description: Marks the package as locally authored. The main repo skips marketplace / signature checks for a dev package; the hub rejects `dev = true` from community submissions.
